members.title: fix(client/sse): release reader lock on disconnect to prevent ~50MB leak
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #1998: The SSE reader obtained via `.getReader()` in `StreamableHTTPClientTransport`'s streamable HTTP client was never released (no `reader.releaseLock()`/try-finally around the read loop), so the reader-tied stream buffer stayed retained after disconnect — a ~50MB leak per long-lived client. Both PRs patch the identical code region (same file, same `while (true) { reader.read() ... }` loop starting at line 328) by wrapping the loop in a try block to ensure the lock is released.

clusters.pick_reason: #2692's changeset explicitly documents handling the batched-POST case: outstanding request ids are grouped by stream, and any id that already has a real response reuses it instead of being overwritten by the synthetic error — #2600's description does not mention batched-request handling, so it risks clobbering an already-resolved response in a multi-request POST. #2692 also settles pending requests with a JSON-RPC formatted error (-32000 'Connection closed'), consistent with the JSON-RPC transport contract, versus #2600's bare HTTP 404 'Session not found', which conflates a session-lookup error with a connection-closed condition. Note: #2600 additionally clears `_requestToStreamMapping` to fix a separate correlation-leak bug in send()/storeEvent() interleaving with close() that #2692 does not address — that fix is not covered by #2692 and should be filed/ported separately if not already merged elsewhere.
